Every number is stated with what moved it and what it did NOT close.
$comment-provenance: THE PROVENANCE HOLE THIS CLOSES (2026-09-01, found by the landing review).
`capture-web.ts` hashes THIS FILE and writes the digest into every cell's
capturePath, so that a capture's optics can be reproduced from what the cell
records. But the optics are not this file: they are the renderer's
DEFAULT_MATERIAL_PROFILE with `patch` merged over it. A constant that moves in
the renderer's defaults and is not named here changes the rendered material
while leaving this file — and therefore the recorded SHA — untouched. Two
different materials then claim the same configuration, which is the exact
failure `capture-web.ts`'s own MATERIAL_PATCH_KEYS comment describes: plausible
numbers, wrong configuration, and no error anywhere.
`sizeOcclusionGain` did this. It was refitted 0 -> 0.05 against the frozen bed
(claims 5.26), the rendered material changed, and this file did not.
Two fixes, because they guard different things:
1. `patch` now names EVERY constant the calibration pipeline fitted or measured
for this profile, not only the ones that happened to differ from a default.
For this profile the patch is still the identity — that is the point — but it
is now an identity that SAYS what it is asserting.
2. `resolvedMaterialSha256` is a digest over the fully RESOLVED material
(DEFAULT_MATERIAL_PROFILE + patch, keys sorted, first 16 hex). It moves when
the resolved material moves, whatever moved it and wherever that constant
lives. tuned-profiles.test.ts recomputes it, so a renderer default cannot
change without either this file being re-recorded or the suite going red.
That is the guarantee the file hash alone could not make.

measurement.fixtures: apps/reference-apple/fixtures — 24 ScreenCaptureKit captures, materialRendered true, deterministic
measurement.fixtureSets: calibration only; validation checked but never fitted; holdout untouched until the freeze
measurement.webCell: chromium 151.0.7922.34, renderer webgpu, samplingBackend gpu-texture, adapter apple/metal-3, srgb
measurement.objective: mean over calibration cells of |Δ interior mean| + |Δ interior stdDev| + |Δ rim peak|, linear light — see packages/calibration/scripts/sweep.ts

cssTierMapping.referenceBackdropLuminanc.previousAdvisory: none — the CSS tier held its own untuned tintAlpha of 0.28 instead of a mapping
method: K5. The CSS tier does not carry the renderer's alpha; it converts it,
because the renderer lerps toward the tint in LINEAR light while the page
composites an rgba() overlay in ENCODED sRGB. cssTintAlpha solves for the
alpha that reproduces the renderer's composite at one declared backdrop
level, and this constant is that level. At the shipped profile it yields a
CSS-tier alpha of 0.781 from the renderer's 0.62.
Fitted against the CROSS-TIER difference (packages/calibration/cli
/tier-delta.ts) rather than against the fixtures, over the 17 measurable
light calibration and validation cells with both tiers captured. Swept at
bRef    ratio gpu/css mean/worst   cross-tier dE mean/worst   css-vs-native dE
0.02 minimises the cross-tier dE on the WORST cell, which is the per-cell
criterion the methodology asks for. The mean is flat across 0.005 to 0.05
(1.10x), so this is choosing the best worst case inside flatness, not
claiming a sharp optimum.
whyCoherenceAndNotFidelity: The two objectives disagree monotonically and in opposite directions:
coherence improves toward the low end, the CSS tier's own fidelity against
Apple toward the high end. They can disagree because the GPU tier is not
itself exactly on the reference, so the point that best matches the GPU
tier is not the point that best matches Apple.
Coherence was chosen. A CSS tier fitted independently against the fixtures
is free to drift from the GPU tier again as soon as either is retuned —
which is exactly how the gap K5 exists to close was opened, by C9a tuning
one tier's constant. A CONVERTED tier inherits the GPU tier's fidelity by
construction and cannot drift without the conversion drifting.
The price is measured and stated rather than hidden: the CSS tier's dE
against Apple lands at 0.0113 where an independently-fitted 0.30 would have
reached 0.0094, against the GPU tier's own 0.0097. All three are well inside
doesNotClose: Exact coherence is unreachable and the arithmetic says so before any
capture does. Matching the two composites for the shipped white tint needs
a CSS alpha of 0.761 over a backdrop at linear luminance 0.05 and 0.635 at
0.8 — a 1.2x spread with no single scalar in it, because one pipeline
applies its transfer function before the blend and the other after. The
measured floor is what remains: cross-tier dE 0.0080 mean and 0.0151 worst,
and an interior level within 1.2% in the mean and 6.7% on the worst cell.
The fitted value is also not the physical reading of its name. The mapping's
FORM comes from the transfer functions, but the fitted scalar absorbs every
other difference between the pipelines too — the CSS tier's saturate(), the
renderer's body-blur LOD chain — so 0.02 is far below any canonical scene's
mean backdrop and must not be read as one.

method: Swept at 0, 0.6 and 1.95 with the tint frozen at the chosen level. The
cross-tier dE spans 0.00791 to 0.00796 and the fixture dE 0.01121 to
0.01131 — a 1.01x grid, the same flatness C9a measured sweeping the GPU
tier's rimAlpha against specularGain. The fixtures do not identify it.
Declined on C9a's own precedent and for one further reason of this tier's.
Dropping the border to zero buys 0.0001 of dE while removing half of what
makes an unfiltered surface legible, and S1's undetectable failure class
says a missed demotion must be a fidelity loss rather than a broken UI.
Winning a flat grid by deleting the feature the estimator measures is
fitting the estimator.
The CSS tier's box-shadow is the one thing it draws that the reference
material does not: C9a measured both sides at approximately zero outside
the contour, while this shadow puts material there. It is what drives the
dom tier's silhouette area to as much as 2.36x the declared component area
and its silhouette IoU to a mean of 0.676 — a measurement of the shadow's
extent rather than of the shape, which is why the dom tier's shape axis is
not gated against the texture tier's thresholds.
Attributed rather than assumed: the IoU mean is 0.6755 to 0.6756 at EVERY
point of every sweep above, moving in the fourth decimal while the tint
alpha moved by a third and the border alpha went to zero. Nothing but the
shadow owns that axis.
Not tuned, because the objective this package fits against has no term
outside the contour, and because removing it is a design decision rather
than a measurement: the repo's effects policy says the fallback is the
design, and the ambient shadow is what makes an unfiltered surface read as
floating rather than as a flat translucent box. Recorded as a parent
decision with the number attached.
Two estimators, and they agree. Regressing each side's interior level
against the backdrop level under the same mask, across the calibration
scenes, gives the material's un-attenuated transmission: Apple passes 0.26
of the backdrop and adds 0.70, where untuned vitrea passed 0.70 and added
0.28. Read as an alpha composite that is Apple ~0.74 against vitrea ~0.30.
The declared objective, swept independently, minimises at 0.62.
The per-pixel affine slope the material axis also reports is a DIFFERENT
and weaker estimator of the same thing: it is attenuated by the material's
own blur, so it reads lower the higher-frequency the backdrop (0.045 on
impulse against 0.419 on photo, for one reference material). The
across-scene regression is not subject to that, which is why the tuned
number comes from it.
doesNotClose: Apple's opacity falls with surface size — implied alpha 0.88 at a 32 px
span, 0.74 at 44 px, 0.56 at 96 px — and this renderer has no size term on
the tint. 0.62 is therefore a compromise across the size sweep, and the
residual |Δ interior mean| of 0.071 is dominated by it rather than by
anything a better single value would fix. A size-parameterised tint alpha
is C9a's parent-impact item.

adaptiveTint.value: both ends white — the backdrop crossover is inert by default
adaptiveTint.previousAdvisory: dark end white, light end sRGB [0.09, 0.09, 0.1]
method: The reference's interior rises monotonically with the backdrop under it
across the whole canonical range (0.680 at backdrop 0.003 through 0.932 at
0.891), which is a fixed tint at partial transmission and not a tint that
inverts against what is behind it. What the reference DOES key on is the
colour scheme: over the same bright checkerboard it sits at 0.809 in light
and 0.055 in dark.
Measured cost of leaving the inversion on: the light-scheme interior-level
error was 0.449 with it active against 0.348 with it inert, before any tint
tuning at all.
doesNotClose: The two ends are global rather than per-variant, so the clear variant
inherits this. Clear has no calibration scenes, so it is uncalibrated
either way — the seed profile already records that as doubly blocked.

method: Swept at 2, 4, 6 and 8 against the objective. The optimum sits at 4 and
beats 8 by 2%, which is inside the flatness of the grid — the whole two
dimensional (tintAlpha × blurSigma) sweep spans only 1.08x. The fixtures do
not identify this constant, and the reason is structural rather than
statistical: no canonical background resolves a step edge at this sigma.
The checkerboard's 16 px cell bounds any measurable window to about one
period, and the impulse background is a sparse train rather than a step.
Moving it would also break a documented relationship — sigma 8 is what
makes core's 24 px samplingPadding advisory exactly the 3-sigma floor S1
measured, and it is what keeps this package and platform-web's CSS tier on
one number. Two percent of a quantity the fixtures cannot resolve does not
buy that.
blurSigma.wouldNeed: A canonical background with one large step edge — a half-dark/half-light field — which is a scenes.json addition and therefore a scope question, not a re-run.

method: Swept rimAlpha at 0.04, 0.09 and 0.18 against specularGain at 0.15, 0.35
and 0.55. The grid is flat to 1.01x — no leverage at all on this profile.
The reason is quantisation. The reference's light-scheme rim peaks measure
0.0003 to 0.0012 of linear luminance on the solid and checkerboard scenes,
while one 8-bit code step at the interior level those scenes sit at (~0.81)
is 0.0079. The signal being fitted is seven to twenty-six times below the
capture's own resolution. Only the photo scenes (0.0080 to 0.0164) carry a
rim above it in this scheme.
Retuning against that would be fitting the estimator, not the material.
rimIntensity.wouldNeed: The 2x profile, which puts four times the samples under the same rim band and lifts it clear of the code step. That is an external gate — a Retina display.

method: The exterior shadow does not separate the two sides: the reference's peak
darkening outside the contour measures 0.0000 to 0.0001 on almost every
calibration scene, and vitrea's measures the same order. There is no
measured gap to close, so nothing was changed.
Note that these two constants do not drive that metric anyway — in this
renderer they scale an INNER shadow inside the contour, which the
interior-level term already accounts for. The exterior falloff the metric
reads is the CSS tier's box-shadow, a different tier's constant.

method: S2 left C9 a question: whether the fixtures support the Apple-direct field
fit or the documented route onto Figma's interpolable axis at smoothing
0.66. They cannot support either, and the arithmetic says why before the
measurement does. S2's own residuals are 6.06e-4 per radius for the
Apple-direct fit and 1.96e-3 per radius for the best Figma route; at the
largest canonical radius (20 px) that is 0.012 px against 0.039 px. Both
are two orders of magnitude below one pixel, and a 1x raster cannot
distinguish them.
The measurement agrees. Contour distance on the corner-bearing calibration
scenes runs 0.00 to 0.14 px mean, at or under the rasterisation floor.
A separate finding makes the question moot on this path in any case: the
platform-web bridge does not forward the corner REFERENCE to the renderer,
so every web surface resolves apple-continuous and the forwarded smoothing
number is discarded. The Figma route is not reachable from the web runtime
today, which is recorded as a parent-impact item.
These three constants cannot be calibrated against the canonical matrix,
and the reason is that THE REFERENCE DOES NOT UNION AT THE ONE SPACING THE
MATRIX DECLARES. Counting connected components in the extracted silhouettes
settles it: the toolbar-group scene yields three separate bodies on both
sides, at 1572/1572/1570 px for the reference and 1769/1765/1756 px for
vitrea, against 1520 px for an unmerged 44 px capsule. Neither side fills
the 12 px gaps — a full fill would add 23% to the group's area, and the
reference adds 3.3%.
So the scene has no union in it to compare. Confirmed by sweeping the
declared mergeDistance across 24, 12 and 4: all three produce a
byte-identical silhouette area of 5290 px, because the union blend never
engages at this separation whatever the threshold is set to. C7's flow-back
assumed the native container would reach 'one merged body' at spacing 12
and built the web side's merge distance around matching that outcome; the
assumption is refuted.
Measuring the union aesthetics needs a scene whose members are close enough
that the reference itself merges them. That is a scenes.json addition, so it
is recorded as a scope question rather than answered here.
incidentalFinding: The same component count exposes something the union hypothesis was hiding:
vitrea's material extends further past its contour than the reference's. Per
capsule, the reference's silhouette sits 0.37 px outside the declared shape
and vitrea's sits 1.73 px outside — about 1.4 px of extra bleed at the 0.02
detection threshold. It is what drives the group scene's silhouette IoU down
to 0.884, the worst of any well-conditioned calibration cell, since three
small bodies make IoU unusually sensitive to a uniform dilation. Not tuned:
the bleed comes from the rim and glow passes together and no single
constant in the profile isolates it.

method: C7's scoping item, and it stands: scenes.json declares no thickness
channel, so the web side uses platform-web's 8 px host default while
SwiftUI uses whatever its material does — a quantity Apple does not
expose. Adding the field to the scene matrix would let both sides honour
one number, but only the web side can actually be set to it, so the field
would pin vitrea to a value and leave the reference where it was. That is
worth doing for reproducibility and worthless as a fidelity measurement;
it is recorded as a scope question rather than resolved here.
Round two of the recalibration cascade, under the protocol declared in claims 5.15
before the fit ran. One constant serves BOTH accessibility profiles, because macOS
force-couples the toggles and both resolve occlusion: increased (Decision Log 8).
Fitted on each profile's own untinted calibration cells against the declared
interior objective; they disagree, and 0.75 is the minimiser of their equal-weight
sum:
lift     increased-contrast   reduced-transparency   sum
doesNotClose: The two references want different lifts (implied alphas 0.945 under increased
contrast and 0.864 under reduced transparency). A single constant cannot serve both,
and separating them needs a reference from a platform that decouples the toggles -
a new capture bed, not a threshold. Also unclosed: the increased-contrast
reference's interior standard deviation, which vitrea does not reproduce and which
dominates that profile's residual objective at 0.18.
